description:
FILED s484b (Opus, 2026-09-13) by the #1117 review probes.  PRE-EXISTING and
independent of #1117: it is the OTHER conjunct of Carp's guard.

Carp.pm:34 / :122 / :124 (the only non-test consumer of `*G{HASH}`) ask

    return unless ref \$_ eq 'GLOB' && *$_{HASH} && exists $$_{$sub};

where `$_` holds a GLOB VALUE (a stash value), not a glob ref.  Probed
5.40.3 vs PCL (scratch/s484b/probe/t4b-conjuncts.pl):

    our %written = (sub1 => 1);
    local $_ = *written;
    ref \$_          perl GLOB   PCL GLOB    agree
    *$_{HASH}        perl true   PCL true    agree
    exists $$_{sub1} perl TRUE   PCL FALSE   <-- diverges
    whole guard      perl 1      PCL 0

So `$$_{KEY}` where `$_` is a glob does not reach the glob's HASH slot.  The
CAST spelling does (`%{$_}` / `@{$_}` resolve to the slot through
`%p-glob-slot-place` â probed working: the Carp.pm:736 spelling
`*{$stash->{$var}}{ARRAY} && @{$stash->{$var}}` answers 1/0/0 exactly as
perl), so this is the ELEMENT-ACCESS path missing the typeglob arm its own
cast has.

CONSEQUENCE: every one of Carp's four guards short-circuits to false in PCL,
which is why nothing has broken visibly â Carp answers "not trusted" where
perl answers "trusted".  No test row is known to depend on it; found while
proving that #1117's shape (B) does not change Carp's answers (it does not â
the guard was already 0 at this conjunct).

FIX SHAPE (untried): the element accessors (`p-gethash`/`p-aref` on a
container operand that unboxes to a `p-typeglob`) route through
`%p-glob-slot-place`, the same one reading `p-cast-%` / `p-cast-@` use.
Rule 11: ONE reading, not a second copy.  Probe the case it would BREAK: a
glob-valued scalar used as a HASH REF today answers empty, so nothing can
depend on the hash being absent, but check `$$fh{...}` on a lexical
filehandle (%p-glob-slot-of-handle's population) before widening.

=== DONE (s484c) ===
SHIPPED 2026-09-14, commit "s484c member 3 (#1726): a GLOB VALUE in element
position is that glob's slot" (runtime-only; no generation bump).

The CAST spelling already worked; the ELEMENT primitives resolve their
container in p-ensure-hashref / p-ensure-arrayref, which had every other
container shape and not this one, so the arm went THERE -- once per sigil,
delegating to the same %p-glob-slot-place reading p-cast-% / p-cast-@ use
(rule 11), with the four fast-path readers gaining a one-line delegation rather
than a second copy.  THE CASE IT WOULD BREAK: a REF to a glob is not a
container in perl and the box model gives a glob value and a glob ref the same
datum, so keying on the value alone silently turned that fatal into undef
(measured: it did, on the first attempt).  %p-glob-referent-p names the
discriminator once, on p-backslash's is-ref flag -- the same one ref() reads.

MEASURED: the task's t4b Carp conjunct table (perl 1 / PCL 1 now), 13 rows of
read/arrow/exists/delete/write/slice/keys on both sigils, the glob-ref fatal on
both sigils, and 10 rows of shapes that must not move.  Guard
Pl/t/glob-undef-01.t 9 -> 10 rows with its Carp row strengthened to the whole
guard, inverse-verified.  ir-spec Â§7.2 is normative.  Residue filed as #1752
(a LEXICAL filehandle in element position: four silent-wrong spellings incl. a
succeeding WRITE, and the three that die leak SBCL's own type error).
subject: Carp guard idiom: `exists $$_{k}` on a GLOB-valued $_ is FALSE in PCL and true in perl (the glob's HASH slot is not the hash a `$$_{k}` element access reads)
